transcript.text: First, inspect the files. for f in ['chart.py','summary.txt','table.csv']: print('=== ',f); print(open(f).read()) continue

The data in chart.py matches table.csv exactly. The defect is the legend. `sns.lineplot(..., legend=False)` creates no labelled artists, so the later `plt.legend(title='Sector', ...)` call has nothing to show. The chart therefore has no way to tell its six lines apart. The summary says each sector is identified by colour and marker, so it needs a legend. Fix: remove `legend=False` so seaborn labels the lines, and keep the existing `plt.legend` call that places it outside the axes. Nothing else changes. After rerunning, I will check the legend labels on the figure. src = open('chart.py').read() src = src.replace(", palette='Set2', legend=False)", ", palette='Set2')") with open('chart.py','w') as f: f.write(src) import warnings with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w: warnings.simplefilter('always') exec(src) print([str(x.message) for x in w if 'ResourceWarning' not in type(x.message).__name__]) ax = plt.gca() leg = ax.get_legend() print(leg.get_title().get_text(), [t.get_text() for t in leg.get_texts()]) print(len(ax.get_lines()), ax.get_title()) continue
